## TL;DR

R 4.5.0 was releases on 2025-04-11 and is now available on Wynton
through the [CBI] software stack. I have validated that almost all
CRAN and Bioconductor packages can be installed with this new version.


## Using R

To use R 4.5.0, which is the new default version, load it as:

```r
{alice@dev3 ~}$ module load CBI r
```

Then you can run R interactively from the terminal using:

```r
{alice@dev3 ~}$ R --quiet

> getRversion()
[1] '4.5.0'
```

To use R 4.5.0 in RStudio, just follow our [RStudio documentation].


## Re-installing R packages

As usual when we move to a new version (e.g. from R 4.4 to R 4.5), any
R packages installed in the previous version (R 4.4) are _not_
available in the new version (R 4.5). This is not the case when we
move from one patch version to another, e.g. R 4.5.0 to R 4.5.1. With
the release of R 4.5.0 we have to start from scratch and reinstall any
packages we need. So, don't be surprised when `library(dplyr)` gives
an error on "there is no package called 'dplyr'". Also, when
installing your first package in a new version of R, R will ask you:

```r
> install.packages("dplyr")
Warning in install.packages("dplyr") :
  'lib = "/wynton/home/cbi/shared/software/_rocky8/R-4.5.0-gcc13/lib64/R/library"'
  is not writable
Would you like to use a personal library instead? (yes/No/cancel)
```

Answer **yes** to this and anything else that R asks you to
confirm. Doing so will make sure you get a smooth ride when using R.
This is all explained in our [R documentation].


## Validation

Just as with previous versions of R available via the [CBI] stack, I
have validated that nearly all R packages on [CRAN] and [Bioconductor]
can be installed out of the box using this new R 4.5.0 installation.

Specifically, I have confirmed that 22,??? out of 22,378[^cran-count]
CRAN packages and 2,??? out of 2,308[^bioc-count] Bioconductor 3.21
packages are straightforward to install. A small number of packages
require some extra love - see our [R documentation] for guidance on
installing those.

The packages that failed to install do so either because they depend
on a system library that is not available on the cluster, or because
they have bugs preventing them from being installed out of the box.


[CRAN]: https://cran.r-project.org
[Bioconductor]: https://www.bioconductor.org
[CBI]: https://wynton.ucsf.edu/hpc/software/software-repositories.html#repository_cbi
[R documentation]: https://wynton.ucsf.edu/hpc/howto/r.html
[RStudio documentation]: https://wynton.ucsf.edu/hpc/howto/rstudio.html

[^cran-count]: CRAN: `nrow(available.packages(repos = "https://cran.r-project.org"))`
[^bioc-count]: Bioconductor: `nrow(available.packages(repos = "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.21/bioc"))`
